items.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020
items.q: then you need to know about Earl Hines.

ctx.x: Dixieland, New Orleans, kind of beboppers.

So some, to make it as a caricature, as some people put, they say that jazz was over when Charlie Parker appeared. And some others believed that jazz was born with John Coltrane in 1961. And basically when they look from now I have the impression that music that I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

love the most is played in between. So anyway, that was the context. So I went to the Hot Club because that was the only thing in my city. The guy was very nice and that was like, that was like a school. Because he used to invite me every week, once a week, and say, “Okay now today we’re going to listen to Louis Armstrong with the Hot 5 or 7, then you need to know about Benny Carter, then you need to know about Earl Hines.
